column1: # Game profile of DARK SOULS: REMASTERED (Switch, update 1.0.3 = v196608; base game v0 not extracted). Plays on the iPhone and the Mac (title, character creation, the opening, the Undead Asylum at 60 fps with sound; 30 on the Switch, rewriter cuts lift its limiter and halve its fixed frame step, patches.py)
# FromSoftware's engine (dantelion2) on SDK 4.5.0, the oldest so far, NVN, Havok, FMOD through AudioOut; subsdk0 is the SDK's movie library (H.264 MP4 movies, decoded by the host).
# Files are in two dvdbnd archives (dvdbnd0.bdt / dvdbnd1.bdt, each indexed by its .bhd5; DCX zlib entries, BND3 archives inside), which the game reads itself

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# the right stick turns the camera and the D-pad switches spells and items; the game maps its buttons by position (B confirms, A goes back)
# only the merged 1.0.3 copy is extracted
# no system resource: the game sets a 3.10 GB heap (pool − used) in the 4 GB layout; about 1.6 GB resident in the Asylum on the Mac
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon
# the rewritten modules (110 MB with main's 51 MB bss) are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory the game takes off the pool for its heap
# 3,099 shaders: 3,040 GLSLC outputs, one per .vpo / .fpo entry of six BND3 archives in dvdbnd0.bdt (shader_split.py bdt_shaders), and 59 more in main. SDK 4's GLSLC writes control
# sections whose +0x20 is 12 bytes short of their length, so the split reads those outputs through their section headers (glslc_section)
